events.title: FDA classifies intraoral cooling device as Class II medical device with special controls
events.summary: The Food and Drug Administration issued a final order classifying the intraoral cooling device (Cooral System) into Class II under special controls via De Novo classification. The device is a prescription-use dental device intended to cool the mouth and reduce oral mucositis risk. FDA determined that Class II status with specified special controls—including thermal testing, electromagnetic compatibility testing, biocompatibility evaluation, and labeling requirements—provides reasonable assurance of safety and effectiveness while reducing regulatory burden compared to automatic Class III assignment.
events.why_relevant: Device classification decisions directly affect market access, regulatory burden, and innovation pathways for medical technologies; Class II status enables future devices to use streamlined 510(k) pathways rather than premarket approval, materially affecting the regulatory environment for dental device innovation.
events.basis: FDA issued an order to the requester classifying the device into class II. In this final order, FDA is codifying the classification of the device by adding 21 CFR 872.5590.
